title: The House of Meditation: Bechet and Ladnier's classical-only flat
summary: Zutty hung out at 129th and Seventh in the place Bechet and Ladnier lived, where only classical records played and a picture of Beethoven hung; Ladnier told Bechet he was the image of Beethoven.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Yes. You'd known I take it, you'd Tommy Ladnier a long time?
Oh yes. Sure. I met Tommy Ladnier in Chicago. Yes, because when he'd taken Louis'
place you know, after Fletcher Henderson, in Fletcher Henderson's band.
Oh yes. Yes. Had Tommy got a, how big a reputation had he got in those days?
Well old Tommy was pretty good.
Yes.
Pretty good.
I always liked the way he played.

Yes, he was good. And I used to hang out in a place, we used to call it, 'The House of Meditation'. With Bechet and Tommy Ladnier. They lived there. We used to all hang out at this spot at 129th and 7th Avenue. And this cot ( EXTRANEIOUS AUDIO INTERFERENCE SUPERIMPOSED ON DISCUSSION ?).
Yes.

And so we'd get up there and they had a professional hobo used to do the shopping for us. And we used to cook and everything you know. And one day we were having dinner and they had a big picture of Beethoven right up on the wall, see. And Tommy Ladnier said, you know something, Bash, he say, you the dead image of Beethoven. (LAUGHTER).
And you never did hear no jazz in there. Nothing but just the Swdn Song!
Oh really?
They never did play any jazz.
Well whose place was it?
It was Bechet and Tommy Ladnier's.
And they played classical music only?
Yes. All the classics man, seldom you heard a jazz record played in that place.
Well how extraordinary!
That's right. And they were Rosicrucianists (Rosicrucianists).
Oh were they?
Yes. Oh they were really deep on that stuff, man.
Both of them? Both of them?
Both of them.
Oh, I never realised there was a serious ......
Yes, yes. Getting back to one of those things, you look like someone, now we played up in Yale and George Brunis told Peewee

He looked like Jonathan Edwards, got a big picture of Jonathan Edwards. And George (Brunis) told Peewee that he looked like him, see it was almost the same you know. Because we were having lunch at that time.
